title: Connected route table (contract 04)
description: Which daemon routes, and which inbound WebSocket messages, each table level reaches through the hub (C-04.13 to C-04.19). Derived row by row from web-chat-dev.worktrees/ae-int/lib/core/remote-policy.js RULES and ANSWER_RULES (with lib/core/element-policy.js FLOOR_RULES compiled into RULES) and from the message types lib/server/ws.js accepts on a socket. The row grammar is remote-policy's own (literal segments, ':name' one segment, a final '*' zero or more segments, HEAD read as GET, case-insensitive, one trailing slash ignored, malformed paths refused), FIRST MATCH WINS and DEFAULT DENY. The rows load into remote-policy classifier() after one mapping (allow is false for host_only and retired, refuse_query becomes refuseQuery), which finds the first matching row; the connector then checks the row's level and requires against the decision itself (C-04.13). The table ships with web-chat in the connector, because it must match the daemon's routes: a separate compiled table, lib/core/connected-policy.js, beside RULES and ANSWER_RULES, which stay byte-identical (C-04.19). The table is keyed by table_version and its sha256, never by a web-chat version. Its sha256 is taken over its canonical JSON: RFC 8785 (JCS), which for this document, holding only strings, integers, arrays and objects, is the members sorted by key at every depth with no whitespace, UTF-8 encoded. In web-chat it is lib/core/stable-json stableStringify(table) hashed with crypto sha256, never stableHash (a sha1) and never a second serializer (C-04.19).

table_version.description: Bumped on every change to any row; the ratchet in test/remote-policy.test.js pins the table's sha256, so a changed table without a bump fails. The connector reports it and the table's sha256 in its hello (contract 05), and a decision names the hub's copy by both (04-policy-decision.json table); the hub logs a skew when its own copy differs (C-04.19). It moves with each alpha that moves a row.

derived_from.description: What the table was compiled from. Informative: the table's identity is table_version and its sha256 (C-04.19).

web_chat.description: Informative: the web-chat build whose tables were read, for example 0.9.0-alpha.2.1. Not a key: an interim build and a tag can share a package.json version (ae/int's reads 0.8.5 until the tag stamps it), so the table is matched by its sha256.

portal_protocol.description: lib/core/versions.js PORTAL_PROTOCOL_VERSION of that build (12 on ae/int, 10 on main 0.8.5). A table older than the daemon's protocol refuses the newer rows by default deny.

source.description: The tree and commit the rows were read at, and the files they were derived from, by path.

grammar.description: The matching grammar: lib/core/remote-policy.js normalize, segsMatch and decide (first match wins, default deny).

session.description: Rows for the chat's surface origin (chat-<label>.<hub>), in first-match order. One row per RULES row, split where one RULES row covers routes of two levels (GET|POST /api/store, * /api/queue/*).

answer.description: Rows for the chat's answer origin (chat-<label>-a.<hub>), in first-match order. Control actions get one literal row each (the action table in lib/server/control/index.js is the daemon's allowlist; the hub's needs the action's level), so an action no row names is refused by default deny.

ws_inbound.description: The viewer-to-daemon message types the connector forwards on a relayed socket, by the level each needs (C-04.18). A type not listed, a binary frame, an unparseable frame or one over the size cap is dropped.

type.description: The message's `type`, as lib/server/ws.js tests msg.type.

level.description: The table level a socket's decision needs for this message to be forwarded.

note.description: Why the message sits at that level.

level.description: status: the heartbeat, below Read, held by every Read holder and by the hub's status reader. read, message, write_page, files: the design's four levels. host_only: never reachable through the hub by any principal in any round (C-04.15). retired: a route the daemon no longer serves (it answers 410); refused like host_only.

methods.description: HTTP methods the row matches, or '*' for any. HEAD is matched as GET.

path.description: The path pattern in remote-policy grammar: literal segments, ':name' for one segment, a final '*' for zero or more.

level.description: The table level a decision needs for this row to allow.

requires.description: Specifics the decision must also carry as true (C-04.5). Absent: none.

daemon_mirror.description: The daemon level the daemon's own second lock needs today for this route, when it checks one (a RULES row's `mirror`, a route's requireMirror, ANSWER_RULES' full). Informative: the connector does not read it. Absent: the daemon checks no level for the route.

refuse_query.description: A query value that refuses the request whatever the decision, read as remote-policy queryHas reads it (GET /api/export/:ref with format=file).

key.description: The query key, lowercased, any qs spelling.

from_rule.description: The RULES or ANSWER_RULES row this row derives from, as remote-policy keyOf() prints it, so a ratchet can check every daemon row is covered.

note.description: A body-level rule the daemon applies under X-WC-Remote, or why the row sits at its level.
